items.summary: Dell published DSA-2026-324 for Dell System Update, the CLI tool that pushes firmware and driver updates to PowerEdge servers. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-86360, is a path-traversal weakness an unauthenticated remote attacker could leverage for root-level code execution; four more high-severity DSU flaws (two remote code execution, two privilege escalation) were fixed in DSU 2.3.0.0. The same week Dell disclosed critical flaws in Container Storage Modules, including CVE-2026-63688 and CVE-2026-63692, both rated 10.0 and affecting authentication around storage-array management. No exploitation or public proof of concept has been reported.
items.title: Critical DSU path-traversal RCE (CVE-2026-86360, CVSS 9.6) and four more DSU flaws patched; two CVSS 10.0 Container Storage Module bugs disclosed
items.why_it_matters: DSU runs fleet-wide on PowerEdge estates, so one unpatched build can leave whole data centers exposed. Ask customers which DSU version their server-update workflows run and whether their CSM/Kubernetes-on-Dell-storage deployments are on 1.18.0+. Good excuse for a proactive check-in on firmware hygiene.

items.summary: At RSAC 2026 Palo Alto Networks launched Prisma AIRS 3.0, pitched at securing the full agentic AI lifecycle (agent identity, runtime security, governance) rather than just observing AI interactions, and Prisma Browser for Business, a simplified secure browser aimed at small businesses with built-in phishing, ransomware, and data-leakage controls. The company also introduced Cortex XCOR, an AI observability platform that automates root-cause analysis for cloud-native environments.
items.title: Prisma AIRS 3.0 for agentic AI security and Prisma Browser for Business for SMBs debut at RSAC 2026
items.why_it_matters: Customers rolling out AI agents are discovering governance and recovery gaps fast. Prisma AIRS 3.0 gives you a presales wedge for discovery around agent identity and runtime controls. The SMB browser is a new door-opener product for small-business accounts where the enterprise browsers never fit.

items.summary: Zscaler announced a collaboration with IBM and Red Hat pairing its Autonomous Application Shield (delivered via the Zero Trust Exchange) with IBM/Red Hat's Lightwell solution. The pitch: vulnerabilities are being weaponized faster than patch cycles, so the joint offering provides inline, application-specific protection while remediation is prepared and validated fixes are delivered.
items.title: Zscaler teams with IBM and Red Hat to shield private apps in the disclosure-to-patch window
items.why_it_matters: Cites Mandiant M-Trends 2026 data that mean time to exploit has dropped below zero (exploited before a public patch exists). Use this in conversations with security teams burned by zero-day patching fire drills, and pair it with ZPA discovery questions.

prompt_of_the_day.prompt: Draft a short, professional check-in email I can send to a customer running Dell PowerEdge servers. Dell published DSA-2026-324 on October 1, 2026 fixing CVE-2026-86360 (CVSS 9.6 path traversal, unauthenticated remote attacker could execute code with root privileges) plus CVE-2026-63697, CVE-2026-71168 (remote code execution), CVE-2026-86361, CVE-2026-86362 (privilege escalation) in Dell System Update, fixed in DSU 2.3.0.0. Separately, Dell disclosed two CVSS 10.0 flaws in Container Storage Modules (CVE-2026-63688, CVE-2026-63692), fixed in 1.18.0. No exploitation has been reported. The email should ask what DSU version they run and whether their CSM deployments are current, offer a quick review call, and stay under 150 words with no fear-mongering.
